themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often shifts while you measure it. So the models start by manufacturing a small set of cases they can actually prove, then grade everything else against it.
themes.evidence: On identity resolution all three models reach for a truth set (freezing a list of people who logged in on two devices, a consented device panel, counting interactions with a verified login), and the same move appears in answer engine optimization's fixed panel of real buyer questions, in incrementality's always-on holdouts, and in the B2B intent work that backtests bought signals against closed deals.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether the evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, how wrong a match is allowed to be. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has budget attached.
themes.evidence: Content governance keeps hitting claims implied by combination and tone that no checker sees, the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions of active customer a political fight rather than a modeling gap, journey orchestration has no agreed price for one more message, and identity resolution asks teams to write down per use case how wrong a match may be.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate and audience caps because sends and spend have no rollback, consent enforcement routes every data exit through a single gate, journey orchestration proposes a shared send log or veto-only kill switch, and the semantic layer work pushes agents through pre-aggregated endpoints with logic baked in.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, a dollar, or a piece of content leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside.
themes.evidence: Consent enforcement answers settle for canary profiles, expiring lists and sampled detection because walled gardens and trained model weights cannot be read back or unlearned, identity resolution notes nobody in the chain is obliged to tell you a revocation failed, ad supply integrity shifts to judging spend by outcomes you observe yourself, and answer engine work can only sample what models say.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by handing it over, and nobody can force them. So the models try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers build a faster declared-agent lane because agents profit by passing as human, identity resolution notes platform owners profit from keeping identity fragmented, incrementality faces platforms that control both the treatment and the evidence, and journey orchestration stalls on channel owners paid for local volume.
